baseline._about: What the learner already knows: an Android developer who knows processes, the main thread, Looper and Handler, the Activity lifecycle, coroutines and garbage collection, and has written a little Swift.

UIKit.def: Apple's framework that runs an iOS app's screens and tells it about its state.

app state.def: Where an app is in its life: not running, inactive, active, background or suspended.

suspended.def: Still in memory, but running no code at all.

run loop.def: A thread's event loop: wait for work, handle it, sleep when there's none. iOS's Looper.

GCD.def: Grand Central Dispatch: Apple's system of queues that run your tasks on threads it manages.

dispatch queue.def: A first-in, first-out line of tasks that GCD runs on its threads.

serial.def: A queue that runs one task at a time, in order.

concurrent.def: A queue that can run several tasks at the same time.

DispatchQueue.main.async.def: Puts a task on the main queue: iOS's handler.post.

async function.def: A Swift function that can give up its thread while it waits: Swift's suspend.

await.def: Marks the point where an async function may give up its thread.

actor.def: An object that lets only one task at a time touch its data.

main actor.def: The actor that protects all UI data: iOS's Dispatchers.Main.

ARC.def: Automatic Reference Counting: frees an object the moment nothing refers to it.

strong reference.def: A reference that keeps an object alive.

strong reference cycle.def: Two objects holding strong references to each other, so neither is ever freed.

weak reference.def: A reference that doesn't keep the object alive, and becomes nil when it's freed.

closure.def: A block of code you can pass around and run later, like a Kotlin lambda.

main queue.def: The serial dispatch queue whose tasks run on the main thread.

garbage collector.def: Android's way of freeing memory: from time to time it finds objects nothing can reach and frees them, cycles included.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what. The lint fails on them (any page text, labels, questions); say the named actor or the plain word instead.

phrases.the system: name the actor: system_server, the kernel, or Binder
phrases.views: say buttons and text, or the screen (View isn't taught)
phrases.lost focus: say: another app is in front
phrases.simply: cut it: it makes a learner who's stuck feel slow
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is
